plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Spreading trees that become clouds of blush-white blossoms before the leaves emerge. Petals drift down like confetti in the spring breeze, and the crowds gather beneath them for hanami picnics.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April, with timing moving later the farther north and higher you go
plants.location: Japan, especially cooler regions such as northern Honshu, where blossoms are still open in early April
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry is a hybrid. Many of the trees lining city streets and riverbanks are clones propagated by grafting, so they tend to bloom in near-perfect synchrony.

plants.name: Lupinus texensis
plants.description: Roadsides and prairies in the Texas Hill Country fill with deep blue spikes of pea-like flowers. Each spike is tipped with a crisp white cap that turns crimson as the bloom ages.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peaks from late March to mid-April
plants.location: Central Texas and the Hill Country, USA
plants.funFact: Texas lawmakers named the bluebonnet the state flower in 1901. In 1971 they extended that status to every Lupinus species found in the state.

plants.name: Nerine appendiculata
plants.description: This is a South African grassland and marsh bulb. In autumn it sends up slender stalks topped with airy clusters of pink flowers that have wavy-edged, curling petals. It often grows in large colonies, and a whole damp meadow can turn pink.
plants.bloomingSeason: December to the end of April (summer into autumn in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
plants.funFact: Nerines belong to the amaryllis family. Their petals have a faint shimmer, as if dusted with tiny crystals.
